why: Both configurations say to connect to mongo-db-showcase-db on the container port 27017, which is exactly the confirmed fix.

Both say to use host.docker.internal instead of localhost to reach the service on the host, which is the change that fixed it. The port is the lab's stand-in, and the extra_hosts note only adds what Docker Engine needs.

The confirmed fix put the containers on a user-defined network with the DB container named dbcontainer. The tool says to use a user-defined network (or Compose), connect by container name, and points out that no container is named dbcontainer, which covers both parts.
Both say to use container_2:8000 (the service name and container port) instead of the published host port, the same as the confirmed fix.
Both say to use ki-backend:8000 instead of localhost:8000, the same as the confirmed proxy_pass change. Restarting nginx is implied.
Both say to call the API through localhost on the port files-service publishes on the host, which is the confirmed fix. 32831 is the lab's stand-in for 6060.

The tool correctly finds that the MySQL container has stopped and points to its logs, which would show the cause. It does not name the change that fixed it (MYSQL_USER root to a regular user), and just starting the container again would fail the same way.

Both say to attach app to authentik_default (external: true) and connect to the server container by name instead of localhost, covering both parts of the confirmed fix. The host.docker.internal alternative is offered as also valid, not as a competing guess.
Both say to connect to db:5432 instead of the published port, exactly the confirmed fix.
Both say to use consul:8500 instead of localhost:8500, the same as setting consul.host to the consul service name.
Both say to publish local-redis's port, which is the confirmed fix. The port number is the lab's stand-in, and binding to 127.0.0.1 or not makes no difference to the substance.

The tool covers publishing the broker's port but not adding a host listener advertised as localhost:<port>. Kafka needs both for a client on the host to work, since the advertised kafka-1:29092 isn't reachable from the host.
Both say to use the postgres service name instead of localhost, which is what fixed pgAdmin's connection.
The tool lists api:5000 (the right target) next to events:5003 and media:9997, plus an in-container branch, without saying which applies. It never names api:5000 as the fix.

The tool points at the right place: the server in primary isn't listening on 9200, so check the command or setting that sets its port. It does not say to add --api-port 9200, and it also offers a wrong branch (another machine).
